text:
maria: heads up — saw a weird p99 spike in last-night's cross-sku sweep (bench-id: bcn-2026-04-12-77). A100 and L40S look fine, H100 shows a ~1.6x p99 regression vs baseline. anyone else see this?

ashok: saw the same. quick numbers from the run summary: A100 p50 11ms p99 42ms; L40S p50 13ms p99 46ms; H100 p50 10ms p99 68ms. total tokens identical.

devon: thanks for flagging. was there a kernel/driver push in the fleet window? cc @li for infra timeline.

li: we had a small nvml bump rolled to h100 pools around 02:10 UTC (rollback later), see deploy #4521. could be correlated. rolling back again for a small group next night is possible.

maria: ok, can we triage asynchronously — i want a hypothesis list and a minimal repro plan. proposed quick checks: 1) re-run single-sku deterministic sweep on H100 with --no-prefetch 2) capture perf counters + nvlink stats 3) run with hot-kv-cache vs cold to see microburst effect.

bench-bot: queued run bcn-2026-04-12-77-rerun (owner: ashok). command: ```./bench-run --sku h100 --model rwl-mid --seq 2048 --batch 4 --trials 600 --tag rerun-1``` expected ~2h. logs will upload to s3://redwood-bench/bcn-2026-04-12-77-rerun.log

ashok: starting rerun now. I'll attach nvml dump and perf counters when finished. will also capture dmesg and power cap from the node. ping me if you want a short live session.

devon: quick code review ping — i opened PR #989 that changes thinbatch kernel selection heuristics. could that affect H100 behavior? @maria can you /grep the commit hash in the bench logs? PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/989

maria: good call. grep showed the commit present in the run logs: commit fa3b9c2. adding hypothesis: heuristic change + nvml bump might interact and increase microburst queuing on H100.

li: infra note — the nvml bump tweaked GPU power reporting; it shouldn't affect scheduling, but it did change driver error reporting frequency. logging spike also seen on a subset of H100 nodes.

devon: if the PR is the culprit we should be able to reproduce with a build that toggles the new heuristic off. ashok can you build with env var THINBATCH_FORCE_LEGACY=1 for rerun-2?

ashok: yes. spawning rerun-2 now with env var and explicit --no-prefetch. command: ```THINBATCH_FORCE_LEGACY=1 ./bench-run --sku h100 --model rwl-mid --seq 2048 --batch 4 --trials 500 --tag rerun-2``` ETA ~90m.

maria: awesome. when reruns finish, please paste small histogram snippet and grep for kernel/queue wait timestamps (we look for >10ms spikes). sample format ok: `hist: p50=10ms p90=24ms p99=68ms`.

bench-bot: rerun-1 finished. artifact: s3://redwood-bench/bcn-2026-04-12-77-rerun-1.log. summary: p50=10.9ms p90=26.5ms p99=69.1ms. nvml log: attached.

li: nvml logs show intermittent nvlink retries on two nodes (node-34, node-71) around 02:12-02:18 UTC. possible noisy hardware causing tail.

devon: ok — two parallel hypotheses: (A) hw/noisy NVLink causing occasional stalls, (B) heuristic/driver combo issuing microbursts. next steps: 1) run rerun-2 with legacy heuristic 2) run rerun-3 on isolated H100 node known-good (node-05) 3) schedule brief dd to repro with nvlink stress. ashok can you tag which nodes rerun-2 hit?

ashok: rerun-2 targeted node-05 and node-71; logs: node-05 p99=43ms, node-71 p99=72ms. so node-05 looks fine with legacy heuristic, node-71 still bad. suggests hardware noise amplified by heuristic.

maria: that leans toward hardware. i'll open an incident-ticket to get node-71 hardware triage and set a temporary host-safety fallback to avoid node-71 in nightly sweeps. ticket: INC-2026-142.

devon: still want to keep PR #989 in draft until we confirm; also add a quick unit test to ensure kernel backpressure doesn't create >10ms queuing under synthetic load.

li: i'll schedule a short maintenance window to run nvlink stress on node-71 tomorrow 03:00 UTC and coordinate with HW ops.

maria: perfect. thanks all. leaving this thread open for artifacts. please post the rerun-2 log and the nvlink stress results when available. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: reminder — if node-71 is quarantined, autoscaler will remove it from H100 pool; notify infra-alerts channel if this impacts capacity.
